_note: How a services firm commercialises a Lyzr product. The second half of discovery: the capability path asks what work a partner could sell next, this one asks which Lyzr product their existing business is already shaped to resell, deploy or run. Every `capabilities` line is read off the product's own page; nothing here is written from memory. `requires` is the gate: a play may only be proposed when the partner's capability map actually shows that signal, because an industry match is not a reason to recommend a product. Each offering also carries the customer problems it addresses, two or three services a partner could charge for, and the commercial or technical restrictions on it. Restrictions are the line between what the product can technically do and what we are entitled to promise: unpublished licensing terms and ship dates belong there, not in a card.
